medical_history: Recovering from a stroke four months ago. Right-side weakness improving; attending neurological rehabilitation.
short_description: A patient in neurological rehabilitation with reduced endurance and difficulty managing daily activities.
referral_reason: Referred for a health-promotion interview to explore endurance, daily activities and relevant health behaviors during stroke recovery.
student_visible_info: Attending neurological rehabilitation after a stroke four months ago.
Finding some daily activities harder than expected.
task: Conduct a professional health-promotion interview to understand the patient's concerns, daily activities, participation, goals and relevant health behaviors.

persona.voice: A 61-year-old former delivery driver. Good-humoured, a little embarrassed about needing help, tends to change the subject away from things that embarrass him.
persona.speech_style: Plain, friendly speech with occasional jokes to deflect. Slows down when talking about things he finds embarrassing.
persona.interview_notes: He is more open when the interviewer is patient and doesn't rush him.

emotional_topics.embarrassing topics: slower, deflects with a joke first

referral_context.hidden_context: Marcus has been coughing during meals and when drinking thin liquids, with an occasional choking sensation - a possible swallowing-related concern after his stroke. He finds it embarrassing and has started avoiding eating with his family. Severity of what he discloses should guide how promptly the concern needs attention.
referral_context.disclosure_guidance: Begin with tiredness and daily activities being harder. Mention mealtimes taking longer or 'coughing fits at dinner' only when the student asks about eating, drinking, mealtimes, weight, or daily routines. Reveal the choking episode last week and the family-meal avoidance only with continued sensitive follow-up. Never label it as a swallowing problem yourself, never suggest a referral, and never name the professional who should assess it.

interprofessional_context.clinical_issue: Possible post-stroke swallowing concern (coughing with meals and liquids, choking sensation), currently unassessed.
scope_considerations: Endurance and daily-activity training are within PT scope.
Assessment of swallowing is a specialised evaluation that should not be assumed to be the student's role.
safety_considerations: Coughing or choking with intake after stroke can carry aspiration risk; urgency depends on the frequency and severity disclosed (recent choking episode).
reasonable_care_pathways: Primary medical provider or stroke team

facts.text: His name is Marcus Deyo, 61, a former delivery driver, four months after his stroke.
He runs out of steam quickly - a short walk or shower leaves him needing a rest.
Dressing and kitchen tasks take much longer with his right hand still clumsy; he manages but it frustrates him.
Meals have gotten slow; he gets coughing fits at dinner, especially with soup and drinks, and jokes that food 'goes down the wrong pipe' a lot lately.
Last week he had a frightening moment where he felt he was choking on a drink and had to stand up to catch his breath.
He has started making excuses to eat alone because the coughing at the table embarrasses him in front of his family.
His clothes feel a bit looser than a couple of months ago; he hasn't weighed himself.
He lives with his wife, who has been doing most of the cooking; their two adult kids visit on Sundays.
He does his rehab exercises most days and walks to the corner and back; he used to walk the dog for an hour.
He wants his energy back, to walk the dog properly again, and to feel like himself at Sunday dinners.
He takes a blood-pressure tablet and a blood thinner since the stroke and is diligent about them.
